answer: The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. A silversmith assay record with hallmark registration works as the gate: a hallmark struck on pieces across many years. The price is per head, and the yarrow test proves it: Each of 379 aliases needs its own assay records, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The shale trail is public, the comet check is cheap to run, and a farm of 379 aliases pays 379 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
